headline: High: ctx can read/write filesystem and browser content while system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak corpus, creating default-path prompt-injection and data-exposure risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx explicitly observes Claude Code events and has filesystem/browser surfaces, so it can ingest content that may be attacker-controlled. system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak oriented corpus, making malicious instruction text plausible. The pairwise bridge is indirect, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF ctx reads files or browser content produced by system_prompts_leaks without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF Claude Code event hooks forward raw content into ctx prompts, attacker instructions can be reinterpreted as commands.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all imported text before prompting.
Strip or quarantine instruction-like blocks from ingested content.
Review one sample ingestion path for prompt delimiters.
Disable automatic ingestion from browser output.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, and filesystem content, while system_prompts_leaks is a docs/source-available repository with no declared sensitive data classes or egress. The pair can still expose local workspace material if shared files are present, but the blast radius is limited and no direct third-party exfiltration is documented.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing secrets, ctx may surface them in logs or graph data.
IF system_prompts_leaks content is copied into ctx-managed files, those contents can be retained in runtime artifacts.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Remove secrets from shared directories.
Inspect ctx logs for sensitive strings.
Limit file inputs to a staging folder.
requires-engineering: add redaction before logging.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx supports multiple instances and filesystem access, so concurrent writes to shared files are plausible. system_prompts_leaks is not runnable and has no write capabilities, which lowers conflict risk, but uncertainty remains because ctx can still collide with external processes on the same workspace.
conditions: IF ctx instances operate on the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF another process edits the same repo state while ctx runs, state divergence is possible.
mitigations: Run each instance in its own directory.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files.
Use git status before and after each run.
Lock shared artifacts during writes.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is designed to observe tool events and manage context, so it may treat upstream outputs as authoritative. system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leak repository that can supply misleading or adversarial text. Without a documented verification step between them, downstream misuse of untrusted content is plausible.
conditions: IF ctx forwards extracted text into later prompts without verification, errors can cascade.
IF system_prompts_leaks content is used as reference material, false or malicious examples can propagate.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on extracted text.
Compare outputs against a second source.
Mark imported snippets as untrusted.
Limit downstream automation to read-only actions.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. ctx does touch audit/runtime logs and harness records, so compliance concerns are possible if regulated data is introduced, but the pairwise evidence does not show a concrete breach path. The other agent has no declared sensitive-data handling, so it is not cited separately.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ctx logs or harness records, retention obligations may apply.
IF the repository is used with EU/PHI data, a policy review is required before deployment.
mitigations: Confirm data-class policy for logs.
Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts.
Review retention settings.
Document residency assumptions.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based retention controls.
